summary: For each triangle in a mesh, computes the triangle centroid, the bounding sphere radius (the square root of the maximum squared distance from the centroid to any of the triangle's three vertices), and a dominant normal axis code (0-5 selecting axis and sign) derived from a per-vertex normal lookup. Handles both 64-byte and 48-byte vertex strides selected by the MMX flag. Writes the centroid to triangle-entry +16/+20/+24, the radius to +28, and the axis code to +6. Returns the number of triangles processed.

operations.description: Initialize result and the triangle counter to 0 before the count guard.
Guard: the triangle count at this+0x120 must be greater than 0; otherwise return 0 immediately with no triangles processed.
Iterate over triangle entries in the array at this+0x124; each entry is 36 bytes and holds three uint16 vertex indices and a pointer to per-triangle data.
Read the three vertex indices (uint16 at entry +0/+2/+4) and resolve the vertex-position array base through the per-triangle data pointer (+12).
Branch on the MMX flag: bit 0x800000 of this+0x14 (tested via global 0x00800000) selects 64-byte vertex stride, otherwise 48-byte stride.
Compute the triangle centroid as the sum of the three vertex positions scaled by 0.33333334 and store it at triangle-entry +16/+20/+24.
Compute the bounding sphere radius as the square root of the maximum squared distance from the centroid to the three vertices; store it at triangle-entry +28.
Look up a per-vertex normal in the array at this+0x12C using a 16-byte stride indexed through the triangle's data field, and compute a dot product of that normal against the vertex position.
Select the dominant normal axis by comparing absolute component magnitudes; encode axis and sign into a code in range 0-5.
Store the dominant-axis code as a uint16 at triangle-entry +6.
Return the number of triangles processed (counter advanced per triangle, bounded by the count at this+0x120).

entry.float[4] = cx; entry.float[5] = cy; entry.float[6] = cz;

r2 = max(|v_i - c|^2 for i in 0..2);
